mentions.story: DigitalOcean leaks customer data between VMs
mentions.text:
FWIW, this kind of problem is minor in comparison to the potential exploits that have and will continue to crop up in shared computing environments.

I was trying to find any cases of a public cloud provider's customer data being leaked or easily visible on the internal customer network, but didn't come up with anything. Somebody's got to do a study on the major cloud providers and see if the good old methods to subvert network routes still works, or if you can easily mitm vm neighbors. (My guess is you can...)

mentions.author: sweis
mentions.story: Technical feasibility of decrypting https by replacing the computer's PRNG
mentions.text:
Here are a few for a start:

- "Cross-VM Side Channels and Their Use to Extract Private Keys" [link]

- "Cache-timing attacks on AES" [link]

- "Hey, You, Get Off of My Cloud: Exploring Information Leakage in Third-Party Compute Clouds" [course]

- "System-Level Protection Against Cache-Based Side Channel Attacks in the Cloud" [course]

In my mind, cache-timing attacks are fairly easily solved, but may be platform dependent. However, VM escapes in general are still a concern.
